data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is a distributional artefact of mutation sampling: when the mutation set is authored by models that had already read the acceptance record, they produce mutations that cluster in the same blind spot the original guards missed, so a test constrains its subject only where the mutation prior overlaps the guard's firing surface.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a fresh, prior-blind mutation set reproduced 3-of-26, the sampling-artefact claim would lose its force.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3 survivors were distributed uniformly across mutation categories, the clustering claim would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the authors' reading of the acceptance record could be shown not to have influenced their mutation choices, the mechanism would be inert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The caveat 'mutations were proposed by models that had read the acceptance record' matters because the mutation prior is not uniform. A biased prior concentrates mutations where the guards are already weak, producing a survivor rate that measures the correlation between the prior and the guard surface rather than the guards' actual coverage. The compile.py 1/9 and every-module 4/4 to 6/7 banding are then the prior's shape, not the subject's.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
